title: Getting started
text: summarize categorical multinomial variables using print_multinomial. , see distribution cancer types treatment responses balanced across dataset. category underrepresented, statistical comparisons may lack power. Binary variables can summarized using summary_binomial. Checking imbalances binary variables crucial. KRAS_Mutation highly imbalanced, conclusions regarding association outcomes interpreted cautiously. continuous variables, summary_numeric provides robust summary. verify distributions symmetric skewed. strong skew might indicate outliers non-normal distribution requiring transformation parametric testing.

title: Getting started
text: Outliers continuous variables can affect statistical analyses. use different methods detect : Different methods different sensitivity levels. iqr method identifies extreme values based quartiles, mad hampel robust skewed distributions. sd assumes normality may ideal skewed data.

title: Getting started
text: Pearson’s correlation assumes linear relationships, whereas Spearman’s rank-based better suited skewed non-linear associations. Pearson’s r differs significantly Spearman’s rho, relationship might linear.
code: mcor_test(clinical_data[, c("CRP", "IL6", "Leukocytes")], method = "pearson") #>                    CRP        IL6  Leukocytes #> CRP         1.00000000 0.05415309 -0.04326444 #> IL6         0.05415309 1.00000000  0.07126276 #> Leukocytes -0.04326444 0.07126276  1.00000000 mcor_test(   clinical_data[, c("CRP", "IL6", "Leukocytes")],   clinical_data[, c("Physician_Score", "Fatigue_Score")],   method = "spearman",   p.value = TRUE,   method_adjust = "bonferroni" ) #> $estimate #>                          CRP         IL6  Leukocytes #> Physician_Score -0.003373907 -0.02593512 0.005017972 #> Fatigue_Score    0.125182200  0.00348041 0.109012944 #>  #> $p.value #>                     CRP IL6 Leukocytes #> Physician_Score 1.00000   1          1 #> Fatigue_Score   0.76154   1          1

title: Getting started
text: significant ANOVA result suggests least one group mean differs. non-significant, fail reject null hypothesis means equal.
code: anova_res <- anova_test(data = clinical_data, Age ~ Country) print_test(anova_res) #> [1] "Anova, F(4, 145) = 2, p = 0.13"

title: Getting started
text: test alternative ANOVA normality violated. significant result means least one group median differs.
code: kruskal_res <- kruskal_test(data = clinical_data, CRP ~ Cancer_Type) print_test(kruskal_res) #> [1] "Kruskal-Wallis, K(3) = 0, p = 0.96"

title: Formats a hypothesis test — print_test
text: x Test object rstatix among anova_test, kruskal_test, wilcox_test. digits Integer specifying number decimal places test statistic. digits_p Integer specifying number decimal places p-value.

title: Formats a hypothesis test — print_test
code: library(rstatix) data("ToothGrowth") res <- anova_test(ToothGrowth, len ~ dose) print_test(res) #> [1] "Anova, F(1, 58) = 105, p < 0.001***"  res <- kruskal_test(ToothGrowth, len ~ dose) print_test(res) #> [1] "Kruskal-Wallis, K(2) = 41, p < 0.001***"  res <- wilcox_test(ToothGrowth, len ~ supp) print_test(res) #> [1] "Wilcoxon, W = 576, p = 0.06"
